description: Replace the throwaway-pty /usage scrape with a direct, passive HTTP call to Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint — same data, no pty, no billed probe, no 5-minute TTL wait.

userStories.title: Read the Claude Code OAuth token from macOS Keychain
userStories.description: As the gateway, I need the same OAuth access token Claude Code itself already holds locally, so I can call Anthropic's usage endpoint without any new auth flow.
acceptanceCriteria: New module src/usage/oauthUsage.ts exports readOAuthToken(): reads the macOS Keychain entry 'Claude Code-credentials' via `security find-generic-password -s "Claude Code-credentials" -w`, parses the JSON, and returns claudeAiOauth.accessToken

Returns null (never throws) when the Keychain entry is missing, the output isn't valid JSON, or there is no claudeAiOauth.accessToken field (e.g. an entry containing only mcpOAuth state) — this is an expected clean-fallback case, not an error
The raw token is never passed to console.log/console.error or any other logging call anywhere in the function — trace every code path that touches the token string
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Fetch usage data from Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint
userStories.description: As the gateway, I want to call the OAuth usage endpoint with the token from US-001, so I can get real-time rate-limit data without spawning a pty.
acceptanceCriteria: src/usage/oauthUsage.ts exports fetchOAuthUsage(token): performs GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage with headers Authorization: Bearer <token> and anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20
On a 200 response, returns the parsed JSON body

On any non-200 response (401/403/404/etc), throws (or returns a clearly-typed failure) rather than returning a fabricated/empty success value — callers must be able to distinguish success from failure
The token is never logged in this function either (same discipline as US-001)
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Parse the OAuth usage response into Conan's existing PlanUtilization shape
userStories.description: As the gateway, I want the OAuth response normalized into the same PlanUtilization shape the pty-probe path already produces, so the UI needs zero changes.
acceptanceCriteria: src/usage/oauthUsage.ts exports parseOAuthUsage(json): returns a PlanUtilization object matching the existing shape in src/usage/probe.ts (fiveHour, sevenDay, sevenDaySonnet: UsageWindow | null; status: 'ok'|'warning'|'limit'; probedAt: number)

Prefers the response's limits[] array (kind/group/percent/resets_at) as the source of truth over the named five_hour/seven_day/seven_day_sonnet top-level fields, per the spike's finding that named fields can be null while limits[] carries the data
Maps limits[] entries to window slots by kind/group: a 'session'-kind entry -> fiveHour, a 'weekly_all'-kind entry -> sevenDay, a weekly entry scoped to a Sonnet model -> sevenDaySonnet
Each mapped window's utilizationPct comes from the entry's percent, and resetAt is the entry's resets_at ISO string parsed to epoch ms (null when resets_at is null)
A missing or null window in the response (e.g. seven_day_sonnet: null) maps to a null UsageWindow slot, never a synthesized zero-value window
status is derived with the same ok < 80% <= warning < 100% <= limit thresholds the existing probe.ts logic uses

Add a unit test using the sample JSON response documented in prd-usage-oauth-endpoint.md's Data model section, asserting the parsed PlanUtilization matches expectations including the null seven_day_sonnet/seven_day_opus case
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Wire the OAuth path into GET /api/claude/usage as primary source with pty-probe fallback
userStories.description: As a user, I want the Usage HUD tab to show fresh rate-limit data automatically, without clicking refresh or spawning a pty, while still working exactly as today if the OAuth path can't be used.
acceptanceCriteria: A background poller (module-level interval in src/usage/oauthUsage.ts) periodically calls readOAuthToken() -> fetchOAuthUsage() -> parseOAuthUsage() and keeps the latest successful PlanUtilization in an in-memory cache, exposed via an exported getter (e.g. getOAuthPlanUtilization())

This entire OAuth path only runs when process.platform === 'darwin'; on any other platform the poller never starts and GET /api/claude/usage behaves exactly as it does today (pty-probe path only, unchanged)
On macOS, GET /api/claude/usage (src/gateway/index.ts:838) prefers a fresh OAuth-sourced PlanUtilization over the existing getCachedPlanUtilization()/pty-probe result when available

If readOAuthToken() returns null, fetchOAuthUsage() throws/fails, or parseOAuthUsage() can't produce at least one non-null window, GET /api/claude/usage falls back to the existing getCachedPlanUtilization()/maybeProbe() pty-probe path completely unchanged from its current behavior, including the existing CONAN_USAGE_PROBE_TTL_MS throttle applying only to that fallback path

The response shape of GET /api/claude/usage (the JSON body: planUtilization, liveUsage, usageWindows, probeError, etc.) is unchanged — ui/src/hooks/useUsage.ts and ui/src/components/Widgets.tsx require no changes
Typecheck passes
